title: Alvin Wall, Ziggy Johnson and Alvin Wall's band
summary: Albert praises saxophonist and bandleader Alvin Wall, mentions meeting Ziggy Johnson in Detroit, and describes the size of bands then; the passage ends in ASR loops.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well very often we do think the same way. Good or bad? Both things. Because if I can't keep up with you, you've got too much depth. Now a man that we've mentioned when the date machine went on, was Alvin Walls.
Great, great saxophone player. Out of Oklahoma City. He died recently in Detroit.

And I just accidentally met him when I went to visit Jay Golson, who used to be a manager in my band in Detroit. And I also met Ziggy Johnson, who was the big director of the first year, was producer from Larry Steele. I always thought that Ziggy was even a better producer than Larry Steele was. He worked with him. He worked with him. Yes I did. Ziggy produced the shows when he was on the plantation club and I told him it was Bill A. Stein. He had come out of Washington, Pennsylvania and was singing with the band. In those days, Bill was all when they were singing semi-ballads and jump numbers like Al Batty Ribbon or something like that. He hadn't concentrated on the style that he has now and the type of songs that he sings now. What about the spelling G?
G-I-G-G-Y. Just the same old word.
There again you have a nickname.
Great. Like we say great, the big around is a balloon.
Was his band a big, loud band or soft, small band? No, he had a good, great band.

What kind, what size did he say? Same size as my band. In those days all bands were equal in size. 14, 15, 16 pieces. Now Father Al has told me about him playing. Who's that? Father Al Lewis. He's a banjo playing, get off that one. Maybe so.
I didn't know the personnel of the, of the, of the, of the, of the band. You knew about the band. He was a band.
He was a band. He was a band. He was a band. He was a band. He was a band.
He was a band. He was a band. He was a band. He was a band.
